# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1483
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1483
- **Title**: [GOAL] herdr integration v2 — fa self-reports pane state via pane report-agent (upstream manifest framing retracted)
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `feat/1481-herdr-v2` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 17
- **Additions**: +1582
- **Deletions**: -38
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T10:36:55Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-14T16:05:29Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1481

## Delivered

**Core (new `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`, pure Dart — no `dart:io`):**
- `HerdrReporter`: fa self-reports its own pane state to herdr via herdr's `pane report-agent` CLI. Gate evaluated exactly once at construction: active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND `HERDR_PANE_ID` is charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` — colon required, herdr's real ids are `window:pane`) AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is absolute + argv-safe AND `FA_HERDR=0` kill switch is off. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no herdr: inert, silent, spawn-free for the process lifetime.
- Static argv vocabulary only: state strings from the `HerdrPaneState` enum (`idle`/`working`/`blocked`), labels from the closed `HerdrBlockedLabel` enum (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/`host-model`), a millisecond seq (wall-clock base so seq rises across agent restarts, strictly increasing in-process), charset-validated ids, and the pinned resume argv `-- fa --session <id>` sent once per session. No transcript text, no user text, no file paths — no code path interpolates anything else.
- Transport is injectable: `envLookup` (host env reads) + `runProcess` (spawn) + `clock` (seq) closures. Fire-and-forget per contract: 2s timeout, silent on failure, no retry, no queue, never user-visible.
- herdr 0.8.2/0.10 asymmetry pinned: the resume argv rides the FIRST report of each session after `--`; state/release/report-agent-session argv shapes are herdr-0.8.2-compatible (older herdr silently ignores the tail).

**CLI wiring (`agent_cli_herdr.dart` part file + hooks in 10 lib files, minimal diffs):**
- Boot `idle` report (pane never sits `unknown`); run start `working` → settle `idle`; every prompt sheet (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/host-model free-text) reports `blocked` with a static label then the post-resolve state via the existing `openPrompt` call sites (6/6 hooked, answer path untouched).
- Release sent exactly once on real quit (REPL teardown awaits it); an in-process session switch (`/session`, `/new`, picker) re-reports the new session via `pane report-agent-session` and re-arms the resume argv — never a release.
- AOT entry (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) passes a `Process.run`-backed spawn + the waiting clock; `lib/` stays `dart:io`-free.

**Docs:** `docs/integrations/herdr.md` rewritten to the retracted framing (pane report-agent self-reporting); the retired skill-install/manifest contract kept only as an unchanged-context section. `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` untouched — all three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) see zero input change (REG-1 verified by diff).

## Delivered vs remaining (owner ACs)

- AC1 state coverage + seq: **delivered** (boot idle, working, blocked ×4 sheets, recovery; ms-seq wall-clock base, strictly increasing).
- AC2 inert gates: **delivered** (truth-table UTs + full-run zero-spawn ITs across every gate miss incl. kill switch).
- AC3 release/switch semantics: **delivered** (release exactly once on real quit; session switch re-reports, never releases).
- AC4 session id + resume argv: **delivered** (id on every report; argv once per session; argv rules validated; 0.8.2 asymmetry pinned in argv-format tests).
- AC5 byte-safety: **delivered** (byte-scan UT over every constructible argv + canary secret/cwd/prompt scan through live runs).
- AC6 docs: **delivered** (herdr.md rewritten; canonical files untouched).
- AC7 kill switch: **delivered** (`FA_HERDR=0` in truth table + full-run IT).
- Remaining (deliberately out): nothing known; herdr-side (multiplexer) rendering is out of fa's scope per the issue.

## Evidence

Gates run locally with a de-quarantined dart-sdk copy inside this worktree (system dart binaries are quarantine-killed on this box — macOS provenance; a `cp -R` of the SDK loses the xattr and runs clean; `HOME`/`TMPDIR` redirected into `.scratch/` because `/tmp` is blocked for this shell):

- `dart analyze` (scoped to all 15 touched files): **No issues found!** — repo-wide analyze has pre-existing errors in `office_addin/` (not this lane) and pre-existing lints at `agent_cli.dart:217` / `provider_models.dart:150` (verified present on `origin/main`, left untouched).
- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart`: **29/29 green** — UT: gate truth table (fully-populated/kill-switch/each-miss), argv snapshots (idle/working/blocked×labels/release/session-switch/resume-block), charset validators, bin-path rules, resume-argv rules (64 args / 8 KiB / apostrophe / control bytes), seq monotonicity under a fixed clock, fire-and-forget throw + timeout silence, AC5 byte scan. IT: boot idle → working → idle → release-once with monotonic seq, AC4 boot argv carries session id + resume block exactly once, `/session` switch re-reports via `report-agent-session` and never releases, five inert-gate cases spawn zero reports through a full run, throwing recorder never surfaces, canary secret/cwd/prompt never leave fa.
- Regression (neighbor suites over every hooked path): `agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test`, `agent_cli_update_session_id_test`, `approval_cli_test`, `session_name_resolution_test`, `agent_cli_run_notices_test` — **29/29 green**.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1483._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `resumeArgvValid` is dead production code — the "defense in depth" claim is false**

This validator is never called anywhere in `lib/` or `bin/` (only the unit tests exercise it), yet the doc comment states the check "exists as defense in depth so a future change cannot ship a rule-breaking argv." It provides no such defense: nothing in the argv builders (`reportStateArgs`, `sessionSwitchArgs`) validates the resume argv before `_spawn`, so a future change *can* ship a rule-breaking argv and only the tests (if updated to match) would notice.

Two clean options:

1. **Wire it in** — validate in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` before including the `-- …` tail (inert on failure, matching the gate philosophy):

```dart
if (resume && resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sid])) ...['--', 'fa', '--session', sid],
```

2. **Fix the comment** — drop the defense-in-depth sentence and document that the rules are pinned by `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` snapshots only.

Option 1 makes the stated guarantee real; option 2 stops the comment from misleading the next maintainer. Either resolves this.

---

### Thread 10 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: typo — "detected server" should be "detached server"**

This PR changed "detached server" to "detected server" in the herdr intro. herdr's defining trait is the *detached* server process (it owns agent PTYs), not a "detected" one — and the sentence is about architecture, not screen detection. One-word revert:

```markdown
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detached server, session restore,
```

---

### Thread 11 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc line is stale post-rework — the transport is no longer a `Process.run` closure**

The rework (kill-on-timeout, per the discussion) replaced the `Process.run`-backed spawn in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` with `Process.start` + a 5s kill window. This docs line still describes the retired implementation:

```markdown
The transport is an injected `Process.run` closure (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`); lib/ stays dart:io-free.
```

Suggest rewording to match the shipped code, e.g. "an injected `Process.start`-backed spawn with a kill-on-timeout window (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`)". Same stale wording appears in the PR description, but the doc is the durable artifact.

---

### Thread 12 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: fire-and-forget spawns can land out of order — pane state can regress until the next transition**

`_spawn` launches each report as an independent unawaited subprocess. Seq is assigned at build time, but delivery order is not guaranteed: a slow earlier report (e.g. boot `idle`, seq N) can arrive *after* a fast later one (run start `working`, seq N+1). Since herdr ignores non-increasing seq, the `idle` is dropped — fine — but the reverse interleaving (fast `working` then slow `idle` is the normal order; the risk is a slow `working` arriving after a later `idle`) can leave the pane showing a stale state until the next transition heals it.

Realistic trigger: boot `idle` immediately followed by a submitted prompt (`working`) — two spawns in the same millisecond-ish window. Impact is transient and self-healing per the fire-and-forget contract, so this doesn't block; if you want ordering, chain the sends (`_pending = _pending.then((_) => _send(argv))`) — still fire-and-forget, but serialized. Worth a conscious decision either way.

---

### Thread 13 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `release()` has no once-guard — "exactly once" rests entirely on the teardown call sites**

The reporter's release is documented as "sent exactly once, on real quit only," but `release()` itself is not idempotent — a second invocation spawns a second `release-agent` report. Today both paths into `_teardownAfterRepl` (`run()`'s finally and `_wireServeTeardown`) are mutually exclusive per process, so the invariant holds by call-site discipline only.

A one-line guard inside the reporter would make the invariant robust against a future third teardown path or a double-invoked shutdown:

```dart
Future<void> release() async {
  if (!_active || _released) return;
  _released = true;
  await _send(releaseArgs(seq: _nextSeq()));
}
```

Defense in depth only — no current double-send path found.

---

### Thread 14 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `Process.start` without draining stdout/stderr — a chatty herdr blocks on a full pipe until the kill window**

The spawn closure starts herdr and awaits only `exitCode`; the child's stdout/stderr streams are never read or redirected. If a (current or future) herdr build prints more than the OS pipe buffer (~64 KiB) for a report, the subprocess blocks on write, `exitCode` never completes, and every report burns the full 5s kill window — one killed process per transition, silently.

herdr 0.8.2's `pane report-*` presumably emits nothing, so this is latent, not live. Cheap hardening:

```dart
final process = await Process.start(
  argv.first,
  argv.sublist(1),
  mode: ProcessStartMode.detachedWithStdio, // or attach a draining listener
);
process.stdout.drain();
process.stderr.drain();
```

…or `Process.run` (which drains internally) composed with an explicit kill timer. Either keeps the kill-on-timeout contract intact.

# herdr integration

[herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr) is a terminal multiplexer built
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detected server, session restore,
remote machines), marks every pane `working / blocked / idle / done`, and
exposes a CLI + socket API so agents can spawn panes and wait on each
other. fa is a supported herdr agent through three seams — the pane-state
reporter (v2, primary), a skill install target, and session resume. The
screen-scrape detection manifest survives as a demoted second tier.

## 1. Pane state — `HerdrReporter` (v2, self-report)

fa reports its own pane state to herdr: a session running inside a herdr
pane keeps herdr's record of that pane true for the whole life of the pane
and releases cleanly on exit. The v1 framing — herdr detects fa by
screen-scraping a detection manifest merged upstream — is retracted: that
manifest never landed in herdrdev/herdr, and a real fa session in a herdr
pane sat at `agent_status: "unknown"` while these docs claimed support.

`HerdrReporter` (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`) owns exactly one job:
reporting the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` to the binary named by
`HERDR_BIN_PATH`. Every report is one fire-and-forget subprocess of
`"$HERDR_BIN_PATH" pane …` with a short timeout, silent on failure — a
dead herdr is indistinguishable from no herdr (no retry, no queue, no log
line, no user-visible output).

**Gate** — the reporter is active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND
`HERDR_PANE_ID` is set and charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`; the colon
is part of the accepted set because herdr's real ids are `window:pane`)
AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is set, absolute, and argv-safe, AND the kill switch
is not engaged (`FA_HERDR=0`). herdr exports the vars to every pane
process,
so the CLI reads its own process env; `FA_HERDR=0` turns the integration
off per-pane or per-machine. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no
herdr: the reporter is constructed inert and spawns nothing for the
process lifetime. A herdr-less machine regresses nothing.

**State machine** (subject: fa's own pane, as herdr records it):

| fa event | herdr state | report |
|---|---|---|
| REPL boot, composer resting | `idle` | `pane report-agent <pane> --source fa --agent fa --state idle --seq <ms>` — sent once at boot so the pane never sits `unknown` |
| run/turn start | `working` | same shape, `--state working` |
| approval sheet visible | `blocked` | `--state blocked --message approval` |
| ask-tool question sheet | `blocked` | `--message ask` |

## PR Description

Fixes #1481

## Delivered

**Core (new `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`, pure Dart — no `dart:io`):**
- `HerdrReporter`: fa self-reports its own pane state to herdr via herdr's `pane report-agent` CLI. Gate evaluated exactly once at construction: active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND `HERDR_PANE_ID` is charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` — colon required, herdr's real ids are `window:pane`) AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is absolute + argv-safe AND `FA_HERDR=0` kill switch is off. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no herdr: inert, silent, spawn-free for the process lifetime.
- Static argv vocabulary only: state strings from the `HerdrPaneState` enum (`idle`/`working`/`blocked`), labels from the closed `HerdrBlockedLabel` enum (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/`host-model`), a millisecond seq (wall-clock base so seq rises across agent restarts, strictly increasing in-process), charset-validated ids, and the pinned resume argv `-- fa --session <id>` sent once per session. No transcript text, no user text, no file paths — no code path interpolates anything else.
- Transport is injectable: `envLookup` (host env reads) + `runProcess` (spawn) + `clock` (seq) closures. Fire-and-forget per contract: 2s timeout, silent on failure, no retry, no queue, never user-visible.
- herdr 0.8.2/0.10 asymmetry pinned: the resume argv rides the FIRST report of each session after `--`; state/release/report-agent-session argv shapes are herdr-0.8.2-compatible (older herdr silently ignores the tail).

**CLI wiring (`agent_cli_herdr.dart` part file + hooks in 10 lib files, minimal diffs):**
- Boot `idle` report (pane never sits `unknown`); run start `working` → settle `idle`; every prompt sheet (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/host-model free-text) reports `blocked` with a static label then the post-resolve state via the existing `openPrompt` call sites (6/6 hooked, answer path untouched).
- Release sent exactly once on real quit (REPL teardown awaits it); an in-process session switch (`/session`, `/new`, picker) re-reports the new session via `pane report-agent-session` and re-arms the resume argv — never a release.
- AOT entry (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) passes a `Process.run`-backed spawn + the waiting clock; `lib/` stays `dart:io`-free.

**Docs:** `docs/integrations/herdr.md` rewritten to the retracted framing (pane report-agent self-reporting); the retired skill-install/manifest contract kept only as an unchanged-context section. `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` untouched — all three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) see zero input change (REG-1 verified by diff).

## Delivered vs remaining (owner ACs)

- AC1 state coverage + seq: **delivered** (boot idle, working, blocked ×4 sheets, recovery; ms-seq wall-clock base, strictly increasing).
- AC2 inert gates: **delivered** (truth-table UTs + full-run zero-spawn ITs across every gate miss incl. kill switch).
- AC3 release/switch semantics: **delivered** (release exactly once on real quit; session switch re-reports, never releases).
- AC4 session id + resume argv: **delivered** (id on every report; argv once per session; argv rules validated; 0.8.2 asymmetry pinned in argv-format tests).
- AC5 byte-safety: **delivered** (byte-scan UT over every constructible argv + canary secret/cwd/prompt scan through live runs).
- AC6 docs: **delivered** (herdr.md rewritten; canonical files untouched).
- AC7 kill switch: **delivered** (`FA_HERDR=0` in truth table + full-run IT).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1483._

> ℹ️ **8 resolved thread(s) excluded; 3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `resumeArgvValid` is dead production code — the "defense in depth" claim is false**

This validator is never called anywhere in `lib/` or `bin/` (only the unit tests exercise it), yet the doc comment states the check "exists as defense in depth so a future change cannot ship a rule-breaking argv." It provides no such defense: nothing in the argv builders (`reportStateArgs`, `sessionSwitchArgs`) validates the resume argv before `_spawn`, so a future change *can* ship a rule-breaking argv and only the tests (if updated to match) would notice.

Two clean options:

1. **Wire it in** — validate in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` before including the `-- …` tail (inert on failure, matching the gate philosophy):

```dart
if (resume && resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sid])) ...['--', 'fa', '--session', sid],
```

2. **Fix the comment** — drop the defense-in-depth sentence and document that the rules are pinned by `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` snapshots only.

Option 1 makes the stated guarantee real; option 2 stops the comment from misleading the next maintainer. Either resolves this.

---

### Thread 10 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: typo — "detected server" should be "detached server"**

This PR changed "detached server" to "detected server" in the herdr intro. herdr's defining trait is the *detached* server process (it owns agent PTYs), not a "detected" one — and the sentence is about architecture, not screen detection. One-word revert:

```markdown
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detached server, session restore,
```

---

### Thread 11 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc line is stale post-rework — the transport is no longer a `Process.run` closure**

The rework (kill-on-timeout, per the discussion) replaced the `Process.run`-backed spawn in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` with `Process.start` + a 5s kill window. This docs line still describes the retired implementation:

```markdown
The transport is an injected `Process.run` closure (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`); lib/ stays dart:io-free.
```

Suggest rewording to match the shipped code, e.g. "an injected `Process.start`-backed spawn with a kill-on-timeout window (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`)". Same stale wording appears in the PR description, but the doc is the durable artifact.

---

### Thread 12 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: fire-and-forget spawns can land out of order — pane state can regress until the next transition**

`_spawn` launches each report as an independent unawaited subprocess. Seq is assigned at build time, but delivery order is not guaranteed: a slow earlier report (e.g. boot `idle`, seq N) can arrive *after* a fast later one (run start `working`, seq N+1). Since herdr ignores non-increasing seq, the `idle` is dropped — fine — but the reverse interleaving (fast `working` then slow `idle` is the normal order; the risk is a slow `working` arriving after a later `idle`) can leave the pane showing a stale state until the next transition heals it.

Realistic trigger: boot `idle` immediately followed by a submitted prompt (`working`) — two spawns in the same millisecond-ish window. Impact is transient and self-healing per the fire-and-forget contract, so this doesn't block; if you want ordering, chain the sends (`_pending = _pending.then((_) => _send(argv))`) — still fire-and-forget, but serialized. Worth a conscious decision either way.

---

### Thread 13 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `release()` has no once-guard — "exactly once" rests entirely on the teardown call sites**

The reporter's release is documented as "sent exactly once, on real quit only," but `release()` itself is not idempotent — a second invocation spawns a second `release-agent` report. Today both paths into `_teardownAfterRepl` (`run()`'s finally and `_wireServeTeardown`) are mutually exclusive per process, so the invariant holds by call-site discipline only.

A one-line guard inside the reporter would make the invariant robust against a future third teardown path or a double-invoked shutdown:

```dart
Future<void> release() async {
  if (!_active || _released) return;
  _released = true;
  await _send(releaseArgs(seq: _nextSeq()));
}
```

Defense in depth only — no current double-send path found.

---

### Thread 14 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `Process.start` without draining stdout/stderr — a chatty herdr blocks on a full pipe until the kill window**

The spawn closure starts herdr and awaits only `exitCode`; the child's stdout/stderr streams are never read or redirected. If a (current or future) herdr build prints more than the OS pipe buffer (~64 KiB) for a report, the subprocess blocks on write, `exitCode` never completes, and every report burns the full 5s kill window — one killed process per transition, silently.

herdr 0.8.2's `pane report-*` presumably emits nothing, so this is latent, not live. Cheap hardening:

```dart
final process = await Process.start(
  argv.first,
  argv.sublist(1),
  mode: ProcessStartMode.detachedWithStdio, // or attach a draining listener
);
process.stdout.drain();
process.stderr.drain();
```

…or `Process.run` (which drains internally) composed with an explicit kill timer. Either keeps the kill-on-timeout contract intact.

---

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

# herdr integration

[herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr) is a terminal multiplexer built
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detected server, session restore,
remote machines), marks every pane `working / blocked / idle / done`, and
exposes a CLI + socket API so agents can spawn panes and wait on each
other. fa is a supported herdr agent through three seams — the pane-state
reporter (v2, primary), a skill install target, and session resume. The
screen-scrape detection manifest survives as a demoted second tier.

## 1. Pane state — `HerdrReporter` (v2, self-report)

fa reports its own pane state to herdr: a session running inside a herdr
pane keeps herdr's record of that pane true for the whole life of the pane
and releases cleanly on exit. The v1 framing — herdr detects fa by
screen-scraping a detection manifest merged upstream — is retracted: that
manifest never landed in herdrdev/herdr, and a real fa session in a herdr
pane sat at `agent_status: "unknown"` while these docs claimed support.

`HerdrReporter` (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`) owns exactly one job:
reporting the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` to the binary named by
`HERDR_BIN_PATH`. Every report is one fire-and-forget subprocess of
`"$HERDR_BIN_PATH" pane …` with a short timeout, silent on failure — a
dead herdr is indistinguishable from no herdr (no retry, no queue, no log
line, no user-visible output).

**Gate** — the reporter is active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND
`HERDR_PANE_ID` is set and charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`; the colon
is part of the accepted set because herdr's real ids are `window:pane`)
AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is set, absolute, and argv-safe, AND the kill switch
is not engaged (`FA_HERDR=0`). herdr exports the vars to every pane
process,
so the CLI reads its own process env; `FA_HERDR=0` turns the integration
off per-pane or per-machine. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no
herdr: the reporter is constructed inert and spawns nothing for the
process lifetime. A herdr-less machine regresses nothing.

**State machine** (subject: fa's own pane, as herdr records it):

| fa event | herdr state | report |
|---|---|---|
| REPL boot, composer resting | `idle` | `pane report-agent <pane> --source fa --agent fa --state idle --seq <ms>` — sent once at boot so the pane never sits `unknown` |
| run/turn start | `working` | same shape, `--state working` |
| approval sheet visible | `blocked` | `--state blocked --message approval` |
| ask-tool question sheet | `blocked` | `--message ask` |

## Plan

### Thread 9 (IMPORTANT) — `resumeArgvValid` dead production code
**Fix: Option 1 — wire it in.** Validate the resume argv in the argv builders (`reportStateArgs` and `sessionSwitchArgs`) before including the `-- …` tail.

RED test: `reportStateArgs(..., sessionId: <>8KiB id>, includeResumeArgv: true)` currently includes the resume tail — a test asserting the tail is dropped for a rule-breaking session id will fail first. Also `sessionSwitchArgs` with a rule-breaking id.

Note: `updateSession` gates charset, but not length — a 9 KiB charset-valid id passes `validSessionId` but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule. So this is reachable in production (state() path: sid from _sessionId; reportStateArgs called with includeResumeArgv=resume). 

Implementation:
- In `reportStateArgs`: `final resume = includeResumeArgv && sessionId != null && resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId!]);`
- In `sessionSwitchArgs`: gate the resume tail: `if (resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])) ...['--', 'fa', '--session', sessionId],`

Wait — should `sessionSwitch()` also skip `_resumeSentFor = sessionId` if the argv was invalid? Consider: sessionSwitch with an 9KiB id — the report-agent-session goes out with `--agent-session-id` but no resume tail. If `_resumeSentFor` is set anyway, then a later state report won't re-arm... but the resume tail would be invalid again anyway (same id). Since validity is a pure function of the id, re-arming wouldn't help — every attempt would produce an invalid tail and be dropped. So marking sent regardless is fine and simpler. Also `state()`: `if (resume) _resumeSentFor = sid;` — resume is computed before building argv. Fine.

Hmm, but wait — where should validation live: in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` (as reviewer suggested) or in the builders? Reviewer's option 1 text: "validate in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` before including the `-- …` tail" with snippet showing `if (resume && resumeArgvValid(...))` in the builder. The snippet is actually inside a builder-ish context. Wiring inside the builders is stronger: any future caller of the public builders gets the guarantee too, and the byte-scan tests exercise builders directly. I'll wire in the builders.

## PR Description

Fixes #1481

## Delivered

**Core (new `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`, pure Dart — no `dart:io`):**
- `HerdrReporter`: fa self-reports its own pane state to herdr via herdr's `pane report-agent` CLI. Gate evaluated exactly once at construction: active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND `HERDR_PANE_ID` is charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` — colon required, herdr's real ids are `window:pane`) AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is absolute + argv-safe AND `FA_HERDR=0` kill switch is off. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no herdr: inert, silent, spawn-free for the process lifetime.
- Static argv vocabulary only: state strings from the `HerdrPaneState` enum (`idle`/`working`/`blocked`), labels from the closed `HerdrBlockedLabel` enum (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/`host-model`), a millisecond seq (wall-clock base so seq rises across agent restarts, strictly increasing in-process), charset-validated ids, and the pinned resume argv `-- fa --session <id>` sent once per session. No transcript text, no user text, no file paths — no code path interpolates anything else.
- Transport is injectable: `envLookup` (host env reads) + `runProcess` (spawn) + `clock` (seq) closures. Fire-and-forget per contract: 2s timeout, silent on failure, no retry, no queue, never user-visible.
- herdr 0.8.2/0.10 asymmetry pinned: the resume argv rides the FIRST report of each session after `--`; state/release/report-agent-session argv shapes are herdr-0.8.2-compatible (older herdr silently ignores the tail).

**CLI wiring (`agent_cli_herdr.dart` part file + hooks in 10 lib files, minimal diffs):**
- Boot `idle` report (pane never sits `unknown`); run start `working` → settle `idle`; every prompt sheet (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/host-model free-text) reports `blocked` with a static label then the post-resolve state via the existing `openPrompt` call sites (6/6 hooked, answer path untouched).
- Release sent exactly once on real quit (REPL teardown awaits it); an in-process session switch (`/session`, `/new`, picker) re-reports the new session via `pane report-agent-session` and re-arms the resume argv — never a release.
- AOT entry (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) passes a `Process.run`-backed spawn + the waiting clock; `lib/` stays `dart:io`-free.

**Docs:** `docs/integrations/herdr.md` rewritten to the retracted framing (pane report-agent self-reporting); the retired skill-install/manifest contract kept only as an unchanged-context section. `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` untouched — all three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) see zero input change (REG-1 verified by diff).

- AC2 inert gates: **delivered** (truth-table UTs + full-run zero-spawn ITs across every gate miss incl. kill switch).

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1483._

> ℹ️ **8 resolved thread(s) excluded; 3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `resumeArgvValid` is dead production code — the "defense in depth" claim is false**

This validator is never called anywhere in `lib/` or `bin/` (only the unit tests exercise it), yet the doc comment states the check "exists as defense in depth so a future change cannot ship a rule-breaking argv." It provides no such defense: nothing in the argv builders (`reportStateArgs`, `sessionSwitchArgs`) validates the resume argv before `_spawn`, so a future change *can* ship a rule-breaking argv and only the tests (if updated to match) would notice.

Two clean options:

1. **Wire it in** — validate in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` before including the `-- …` tail (inert on failure, matching the gate philosophy):

```dart
if (resume && resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sid])) ...['--', 'fa', '--session', sid],
```

2. **Fix the comment** — drop the defense-in-depth sentence and document that the rules are pinned by `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` snapshots only.

Option 1 makes the stated guarantee real; option 2 stops the comment from misleading the next maintainer. Either resolves this.

---

### Thread 10 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: typo — "detected server" should be "detached server"**

This PR changed "detached server" to "detected server" in the herdr intro. herdr's defining trait is the *detached* server process (it owns agent PTYs), not a "detected" one — and the sentence is about architecture, not screen detection. One-word revert:

```markdown
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detached server, session restore,
```

---

### Thread 11 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc line is stale post-rework — the transport is no longer a `Process.run` closure**

The rework (kill-on-timeout, per the discussion) replaced the `Process.run`-backed spawn in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` with `Process.start` + a 5s kill window. This docs line still describes the retired implementation:

```markdown
The transport is an injected `Process.run` closure (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`); lib/ stays dart:io-free.
```

Suggest rewording to match the shipped code, e.g. "an injected `Process.start`-backed spawn with a kill-on-timeout window (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`)". Same stale wording appears in the PR description, but the doc is the durable artifact.

---

### Thread 12 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: fire-and-forget spawns can land out of order — pane state can regress until the next transition**

`_spawn` launches each report as an independent unawaited subprocess. Seq is assigned at build time, but delivery order is not guaranteed: a slow earlier report (e.g. boot `idle`, seq N) can arrive *after* a fast later one (run start `working`, seq N+1). Since herdr ignores non-increasing seq, the `idle` is dropped — fine — but the reverse interleaving (fast `working` then slow `idle` is the normal order; the risk is a slow `working` arriving after a later `idle`) can leave the pane showing a stale state until the next transition heals it.

Realistic trigger: boot `idle` immediately followed by a submitted prompt (`working`) — two spawns in the same millisecond-ish window. Impact is transient and self-healing per the fire-and-forget contract, so this doesn't block; if you want ordering, chain the sends (`_pending = _pending.then((_) => _send(argv))`) — still fire-and-forget, but serialized. Worth a conscious decision either way.

---

### Thread 13 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `release()` has no once-guard — "exactly once" rests entirely on the teardown call sites**

The reporter's release is documented as "sent exactly once, on real quit only," but `release()` itself is not idempotent — a second invocation spawns a second `release-agent` report. Today both paths into `_teardownAfterRepl` (`run()`'s finally and `_wireServeTeardown`) are mutually exclusive per process, so the invariant holds by call-site discipline only.

A one-line guard inside the reporter would make the invariant robust against a future third teardown path or a double-invoked shutdown:

```dart
Future<void> release() async {
  if (!_active || _released) return;
  _released = true;
  await _send(releaseArgs(seq: _nextSeq()));
}
```

Defense in depth only — no current double-send path found.

---

### Thread 14 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):

Fixes #1481

**Core (new `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`, pure Dart — no `dart:io`):**
- `HerdrReporter`: fa self-reports its own pane state to herdr via herdr's `pane report-agent` CLI. Gate evaluated exactly once at construction: active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND `HERDR_PANE_ID` is charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` — colon required, herdr's real ids are `window:pane`) AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is absolute + argv-safe AND `FA_HERDR=0` kill switch is off. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no herdr: inert, silent, spawn-free for the process lifetime.
- Static argv vocabulary only: state strings from the `HerdrPaneState` enum (`idle`/`working`/`blocked`), labels from the closed `HerdrBlockedLabel` enum (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/`host-model`), a millisecond seq (wall-clock base so seq rises across agent restarts, strictly increasing in-process), charset-validated ids, and the pinned resume argv `-- fa --session <id>` sent once per session. No transcript text, no user text, no file paths — no code path interpolates anything else.
- Transport is injectable: `envLookup` (host env reads) + `runProcess` (spawn) + `clock` (seq) closures. Fire-and-forget per contract: 2s timeout, silent on failure, no retry, no queue, never user-visible.

**CLI wiring (`agent_cli_herdr.dart` part file + hooks in 10 lib files, minimal diffs):**

# herdr integration

[herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr) is a terminal multiplexer built
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detected server, session restore,
remote machines), marks every pane `working / blocked / idle / done`, and
exposes a CLI + socket API so agents can spawn panes and wait on each
other. fa is a supported herdr agent through three seams — the pane-state
reporter (v2, primary), a skill install target, and session resume. The
screen-scrape detection manifest survives as a demoted second tier.

## 1. Pane state — `HerdrReporter` (v2, self-report)

fa reports its own pane state to herdr: a session running inside a herdr
pane keeps herdr's record of that pane true for the whole life of the pane
and releases cleanly on exit. The v1 framing — herdr detects fa by
screen-scraping a detection manifest merged upstream — is retracted: that
manifest never landed in herdrdev/herdr, and a real fa session in a herdr
pane sat at `agent_status: "unknown"` while these docs claimed support.

`HerdrReporter` (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`) owns exactly one job:
reporting the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` to the binary named by
`HERDR_BIN_PATH`. Every report is one fire-and-forget subprocess of
`"$HERDR_BIN_PATH" pane …` with a short timeout, silent on failure — a
dead herdr is indistinguishable from no herdr (no retry, no queue, no log
line, no user-visible output).

**Gate** — the reporter is active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND
`HERDR_PANE_ID` is set and charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`; the colon
is part of the accepted set because herdr's real ids are `window:pane`)
AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is set, absolute, and argv-safe, AND the kill switch
is not engaged (`FA_HERDR=0`). herdr exports the vars to every pane
process,
so the CLI reads its own process env; `FA_HERDR=0` turns the integration
off per-pane or per-machine. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no
herdr: the reporter is constructed inert and spawns nothing for the
process lifetime. A herdr-less machine regresses nothing.

**State machine** (subject: fa's own pane, as herdr records it):

| fa event | herdr state | report |
|---|---|---|
| REPL boot, composer resting | `idle` | `pane report-agent <pane> --source fa --agent fa --state idle --seq <ms>` — sent once at boot so the pane never sits `unknown` |
| run/turn start | `working` | same shape, `--state working` |
| approval sheet visible | `blocked` | `--state blocked --message approval` |
| ask-tool question sheet | `blocked` | `--message ask` |

## PR Description

Fixes #1481

## Delivered

**Core (new `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`, pure Dart — no `dart:io`):**
- `HerdrReporter`: fa self-reports its own pane state to herdr via herdr's `pane report-agent` CLI. Gate evaluated exactly once at construction: active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND `HERDR_PANE_ID` is charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` — colon required, herdr's real ids are `window:pane`) AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is absolute + argv-safe AND `FA_HERDR=0` kill switch is off. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no herdr: inert, silent, spawn-free for the process lifetime.
- Static argv vocabulary only: state strings from the `HerdrPaneState` enum (`idle`/`working`/`blocked`), labels from the closed `HerdrBlockedLabel` enum (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/`host-model`), a millisecond seq (wall-clock base so seq rises across agent restarts, strictly increasing in-process), charset-validated ids, and the pinned resume argv `-- fa --session <id>` sent once per session. No transcript text, no user text, no file paths — no code path interpolates anything else.
- Transport is injectable: `envLookup` (host env reads) + `runProcess` (spawn) + `clock` (seq) closures. Fire-and-forget per contract: 2s timeout, silent on failure, no retry, no queue, never user-visible.
- herdr 0.8.2/0.10 asymmetry pinned: the resume argv rides the FIRST report of each session after `--`; state/release/report-agent-session argv shapes are herdr-0.8.2-compatible (older herdr silently ignores the tail).

**CLI wiring (`agent_cli_herdr.dart` part file + hooks in 10 lib files, minimal diffs):**
- Boot `idle` report (pane never sits `unknown`); run start `working` → settle `idle`; every prompt sheet (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/host-model free-text) reports `blocked` with a static label then the post-resolve state via the existing `openPrompt` call sites (6/6 hooked, answer path untouched).
- Release sent exactly once on real quit (REPL teardown awaits it); an in-process session switch (`/session`, `/new`, picker) re-reports the new session via `pane report-agent-session` and re-arms the resume argv — never a release.
- AOT entry (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) passes a `Process.run`-backed spawn + the waiting clock; `lib/` stays `dart:io`-free.

**Docs:** `docs/integrations/herdr.md` rewritten to the retracted framing (pane report-agent self-reporting); the retired skill-install/manifest contract kept only as an unchanged-context section. `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` untouched — all three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) see zero input change (REG-1 verified by diff).

## Delivered vs remaining (owner ACs)

- AC1 state coverage + seq: **delivered** (boot idle, working, blocked ×4 sheets, recovery; ms-seq wall-clock base, strictly increasing).
- AC2 inert gates: **delivered** (truth-table UTs + full-run zero-spawn ITs across every gate miss incl. kill switch).
- AC3 release/switch semantics: **delivered** (release exactly once on real quit; session switch re-reports, never releases).
- AC4 session id + resume argv: **delivered** (id on every report; argv once per session; argv rules validated; 0.8.2 asymmetry pinned in argv-format tests).
- AC5 byte-safety: **delivered** (byte-scan UT over every constructible argv + canary secret/cwd/prompt scan through live runs).
- AC6 docs: **delivered** (herdr.md rewritten; canonical files untouched).
- AC7 kill switch: **delivered** (`FA_HERDR=0` in truth table + full-run IT).
- Remaining (deliberately out): nothing known; herdr-side (multiplexer) rendering is out of fa's scope per the issue.

## Evidence

Gates run locally with a de-quarantined dart-sdk copy inside this worktree (system dart binaries are quarantine-killed on this box — macOS provenance; a `cp -R` of the SDK loses the xattr and runs clean; `HOME`/`TMPDIR` redirected into `.scratch/` because `/tmp` is blocked for this shell):

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1483._

> ℹ️ **8 resolved thread(s) excluded; 3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `resumeArgvValid` is dead production code — the "defense in depth" claim is false**

This validator is never called anywhere in `lib/` or `bin/` (only the unit tests exercise it), yet the doc comment states the check "exists as defense in depth so a future change cannot ship a rule-breaking argv." It provides no such defense: nothing in the argv builders (`reportStateArgs`, `sessionSwitchArgs`) validates the resume argv before `_spawn`, so a future change *can* ship a rule-breaking argv and only the tests (if updated to match) would notice.

Two clean options:

1. **Wire it in** — validate in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` before including the `-- …` tail (inert on failure, matching the gate philosophy):

```dart
if (resume && resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sid])) ...['--', 'fa', '--session', sid],
```

2. **Fix the comment** — drop the defense-in-depth sentence and document that the rules are pinned by `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` snapshots only.

Option 1 makes the stated guarantee real; option 2 stops the comment from misleading the next maintainer. Either resolves this.

---

### Thread 10 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: typo — "detected server" should be "detached server"**

This PR changed "detached server" to "detected server" in the herdr intro. herdr's defining trait is the *detached* server process (it owns agent PTYs), not a "detected" one — and the sentence is about architecture, not screen detection. One-word revert:

```markdown
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detached server, session restore,
```

---

### Thread 11 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc line is stale post-rework — the transport is no longer a `Process.run` closure**

The rework (kill-on-timeout, per the discussion) replaced the `Process.run`-backed spawn in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` with `Process.start` + a 5s kill window. This docs line still describes the retired implementation:

```markdown
The transport is an injected `Process.run` closure (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`); lib/ stays dart:io-free.
```

Suggest rewording to match the shipped code, e.g. "an injected `Process.start`-backed spawn with a kill-on-timeout window (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`)". Same stale wording appears in the PR description, but the doc is the durable artifact.

---

### Thread 12 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: fire-and-forget spawns can land out of order — pane state can regress until the next transition**

`_spawn` launches each report as an independent unawaited subprocess. Seq is assigned at build time, but delivery order is not guaranteed: a slow earlier report (e.g. boot `idle`, seq N) can arrive *after* a fast later one (run start `working`, seq N+1). Since herdr ignores non-increasing seq, the `idle` is dropped — fine — but the reverse interleaving (fast `working` then slow `idle` is the normal order; the risk is a slow `working` arriving after a later `idle`) can leave the pane showing a stale state until the next transition heals it.

Realistic trigger: boot `idle` immediately followed by a submitted prompt (`working`) — two spawns in the same millisecond-ish window. Impact is transient and self-healing per the fire-and-forget contract, so this doesn't block; if you want ordering, chain the sends (`_pending = _pending.then((_) => _send(argv))`) — still fire-and-forget, but serialized. Worth a conscious decision either way.

---

### Thread 13 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `release()` has no once-guard — "exactly once" rests entirely on the teardown call sites**

The reporter's release is documented as "sent exactly once, on real quit only," but `release()` itself is not idempotent — a second invocation spawns a second `release-agent` report. Today both paths into `_teardownAfterRepl` (`run()`'s finally and `_wireServeTeardown`) are mutually exclusive per process, so the invariant holds by call-site discipline only.

A one-line guard inside the reporter would make the invariant robust against a future third teardown path or a double-invoked shutdown:

```dart
Future<void> release() async {
  if (!_active || _released) return;
  _released = true;
  await _send(releaseArgs(seq: _nextSeq()));
}
```

Defense in depth only — no current double-send path found.

---

### Thread 14 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `Process.start` without draining stdout/stderr — a chatty herdr blocks on a full pipe until the kill window**

The spawn closure starts herdr and awaits only `exitCode`; the child's stdout/stderr streams are never read or redirected. If a (current or future) herdr build prints more than the OS pipe buffer (~64 KiB) for a report, the subprocess blocks on write, `exitCode` never completes, and every report burns the full 5s kill window — one killed process per transition, silently.

herdr 0.8.2's `pane report-*` presumably emits nothing, so this is latent, not live. Cheap hardening:

```dart
final process = await Process.start(
  argv.first,
  argv.sublist(1),
  mode: ProcessStartMode.detachedWithStdio, // or attach a draining listener
);
process.stdout.drain();
process.stderr.drain();
```

…or `Process.run` (which drains internally) composed with an explicit kill timer. Either keeps the kill-on-timeout contract intact.

---

### Thread 15

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Next Steps**:

2. Fix the two doc/comment inaccuracies and consider killing the spawned process on timeout.

**Core (new `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`, pure Dart — no `dart:io`):**
- `HerdrReporter`: fa self-reports its own pane state to herdr via herdr's `pane report-agent` CLI. Gate evaluated exactly once at construction: active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND `HERDR_PANE_ID` is charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` — colon required, herdr's real ids are `window:pane`) AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is absolute + argv-safe AND `FA_HERDR=0` kill switch is off. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no herdr: inert, silent, spawn-free for the process lifetime.
- Static argv vocabulary only: state strings from the `HerdrPaneState` enum (`idle`/`working`/`blocked`), labels from the closed `HerdrBlockedLabel` enum (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/`host-model`), a millisecond seq (wall-clock base so seq rises across agent restarts, strictly increasing in-process), charset-validated ids, and the pinned resume argv `-- fa --session <id>` sent once per session. # herdr integration

[herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr) is a terminal multiplexer built
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detected server, session restore,
remote machines), marks every pane `working / blocked / idle / done`, and
exposes a CLI + socket API so agents can spawn panes and wait on each
other. fa is a supported herdr agent through three seams — the pane-state
reporter (v2, primary), a skill install target, and session resume. The
screen-scrape detection manifest survives as a demoted second tier.

## 1. Pane state — `HerdrReporter` (v2, self-report)

fa reports its own pane state to herdr: a session running inside a herdr
pane keeps herdr's record of that pane true for the whole life of the pane
and releases cleanly on exit. The v1 framing — herdr detects fa by
screen-scraping a detection manifest merged upstream — is retracted: that
manifest never landed in herdrdev/herdr, and a real fa session in a herdr
pane sat at `agent_status: "unknown"` while these docs claimed support.

`HerdrReporter` (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`) owns exactly one job:
reporting the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` to the binary named by
`HERDR_BIN_PATH`. Every report is one fire-and-forget subprocess of
`"$HERDR_BIN_PATH" pane …` with a short timeout, silent on failure — a
dead herdr is indistinguishable from no herdr (no retry, no queue, no log
line, no user-visible output).

**Gate** — the reporter is active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND
`HERDR_PANE_ID` is set and charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`; the colon
is part of the accepted set because herdr's real ids are `window:pane`)
AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is set, absolute, and argv-safe, AND the kill switch
is not engaged (`FA_HERDR=0`). herdr exports the vars to every pane
process,
so the CLI reads its own process env; `FA_HERDR=0` turns the integration
off per-pane or per-machine. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no
herdr: the reporter is constructed inert and spawns nothing for the
process lifetime. A herdr-less machine regresses nothing.

**State machine** (subject: fa's own pane, as herdr records it):

| fa event | herdr state | report |
|---|---|---|
| REPL boot, composer resting | `idle` | `pane report-agent <pane> --source fa --agent fa --state idle --seq <ms>` — sent once at boot so the pane never sits `unknown` |
| run/turn start | `working` | same shape, `--state working` |
| approval sheet visible | `blocked` | `--state blocked --message approval` |
| ask-tool question sheet | `blocked` | `--message ask` |

## Plan

### Thread 9 (IMPORTANT) — `resumeArgvValid` dead production code
**Fix: Option 1 — wire it in.** Validate the resume argv in the argv builders (`reportStateArgs` and `sessionSwitchArgs`) before including the `-- …` tail.

RED test: `reportStateArgs(..., sessionId: <>8KiB id>, includeResumeArgv: true)` currently includes the resume tail — a test asserting the tail is dropped for a rule-breaking session id will fail first. Also `sessionSwitchArgs` with a rule-breaking id.

Note: `updateSession` gates charset, but not length — a 9 KiB charset-valid id passes `validSessionId` but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule. So this is reachable in production (state() path: sid from _sessionId; reportStateArgs called with includeResumeArgv=resume). 

Implementation:
- In `reportStateArgs`: `final resume = includeResumeArgv && sessionId != null && resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId!]);`
- In `sessionSwitchArgs`: gate the resume tail: `if (resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])) ...['--', 'fa', '--session', sessionId],`

Wait — should `sessionSwitch()` also skip `_resumeSentFor = sessionId` if the argv was invalid? Consider: sessionSwitch with an 9KiB id — the report-agent-session goes out with `--agent-session-id` but no resume tail. If `_resumeSentFor` is set anyway, then a later state report won't re-arm... but the resume tail would be invalid again anyway (same id). Since validity is a pure function of the id, re-arming wouldn't help — every attempt would produce an invalid tail and be dropped. So marking sent regardless is fine and simpler. Also `state()`: `if (resume) _resumeSentFor = sid;` — resume is computed before building argv. Fine.

Hmm, but wait — where should validation live: in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` (as reviewer suggested) or in the builders? Reviewer's option 1 text: "validate in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` before including the `-- …` tail" with snippet showing `if (resume && resumeArgvValid(...))` in the builder. The snippet is actually inside a builder-ish context. Wiring inside the builders is stronger: any future caller of the public builders gets the guarantee too, and the byte-scan tests exercise builders directly. I'll wire in the builders.

### Thread 12 (suggestion) — out-of-order delivery
**Fix: serialize delivery via a `_pending` chain.** `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` spawn through `_spawn` which chains onto `_pending`. `release()` also rides the chain (and awaits it, preserving the REPL-teardown-await contract).

RED test (UT): a recorder whose first call blocks on a Completer: call state(idle) then state(working); assert sink has 1 entry; complete; pump; assert 2 entries in order.

Also lifecycle: seq strictly increasing already tested.

Careful with `_nextSeq()` timing: seq is assigned at build/enqueue time. With chaining, send order == enqueue order == seq order.

  if (!_active || _released) return;

## PR Description

Fixes #1481

## Delivered

**Core (new `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`, pure Dart — no `dart:io`):**
- `HerdrReporter`: fa self-reports its own pane state to herdr via herdr's `pane report-agent` CLI. Gate evaluated exactly once at construction: active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND `HERDR_PANE_ID` is charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+` — colon required, herdr's real ids are `window:pane`) AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is absolute + argv-safe AND `FA_HERDR=0` kill switch is off. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no herdr: inert, silent, spawn-free for the process lifetime.
- Static argv vocabulary only: state strings from the `HerdrPaneState` enum (`idle`/`working`/`blocked`), labels from the closed `HerdrBlockedLabel` enum (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/`host-model`), a millisecond seq (wall-clock base so seq rises across agent restarts, strictly increasing in-process), charset-validated ids, and the pinned resume argv `-- fa --session <id>` sent once per session. No transcript text, no user text, no file paths — no code path interpolates anything else.
- Transport is injectable: `envLookup` (host env reads) + `runProcess` (spawn) + `clock` (seq) closures. Fire-and-forget per contract: 2s timeout, silent on failure, no retry, no queue, never user-visible.
- herdr 0.8.2/0.10 asymmetry pinned: the resume argv rides the FIRST report of each session after `--`; state/release/report-agent-session argv shapes are herdr-0.8.2-compatible (older herdr silently ignores the tail).

**CLI wiring (`agent_cli_herdr.dart` part file + hooks in 10 lib files, minimal diffs):**
- Boot `idle` report (pane never sits `unknown`); run start `working` → settle `idle`; every prompt sheet (`approval`/`ask`/`secret`/host-model free-text) reports `blocked` with a static label then the post-resolve state via the existing `openPrompt` call sites (6/6 hooked, answer path untouched).
- Release sent exactly once on real quit (REPL teardown awaits it); an in-process session switch (`/session`, `/new`, picker) re-reports the new session via `pane report-agent-session` and re-arms the resume argv — never a release.
- AOT entry (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`) passes a `Process.run`-backed spawn + the waiting clock; `lib/` stays `dart:io`-free.

**Docs:** `docs/integrations/herdr.md` rewritten to the retracted framing (pane report-agent self-reporting); the retired skill-install/manifest contract kept only as an unchanged-context section. `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` untouched — all three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) see zero input change (REG-1 verified by diff).

## Delivered vs remaining (owner ACs)

- AC1 state coverage + seq: **delivered** (boot idle, working, blocked ×4 sheets, recovery; ms-seq wall-clock base, strictly increasing).
- AC2 inert gates: **delivered** (truth-table UTs + full-run zero-spawn ITs across every gate miss incl. kill switch).
- AC3 release/switch semantics: **delivered** (release exactly once on real quit; session switch re-reports, never releases).
- AC4 session id + resume argv: **delivered** (id on every report; argv once per session; argv rules validated; 0.8.2 asymmetry pinned in argv-format tests).
- AC5 byte-safety: **delivered** (byte-scan UT over every constructible argv + canary secret/cwd/prompt scan through live runs).
- AC6 docs: **delivered** (herdr.md rewritten; canonical files untouched).
- AC7 kill switch: **delivered** (`FA_HERDR=0` in truth table + full-run IT).
- Remaining (deliberately out): nothing known; herdr-side (multiplexer) rendering is out of fa's scope per the issue.

## Evidence

Gates run locally with a de-quarantined dart-sdk copy inside this worktree (system dart binaries are quarantine-killed on this box — macOS provenance; a `cp -R` of the SDK loses the xattr and runs clean; `HOME`/`TMPDIR` redirected into `.scratch/` because `/tmp` is blocked for this shell):

- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart`: **29/29 green** — UT: gate truth table (fully-populated/kill-switch/each-miss), argv snapshots (idle/working/blocked×labels/release/session-switch/resume-block), charset validators, bin-path rules, resume-argv rules (64 args / 8 KiB / apostrophe / control bytes), seq monotonicity under a fixed clock, fire-and-forget throw + timeout silence, AC5 byte scan. IT: boot idle → working → idle → release-once with monotonic seq, AC4 boot argv carries session id + resume block exactly once, `/session` switch re-reports via `report-agent-session` and never releases, five inert-gate cases spawn zero reports through a full run, throwing recorder never surfaces, canary secret/cwd/prompt never leave fa.
- Regression (neighbor suites over every hooked path): `agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test`, `agent_cli_update_session_id_test`, `approval_cli_test`, `session_name_resolution_test`, `agent_cli_run_notices_test` — **29/29 green**.

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1483._

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `resumeArgvValid` is dead production code — the "defense in depth" claim is false**

This validator is never called anywhere in `lib/` or `bin/` (only the unit tests exercise it), yet the doc comment states the check "exists as defense in depth so a future change cannot ship a rule-breaking argv." It provides no such defense: nothing in the argv builders (`reportStateArgs`, `sessionSwitchArgs`) validates the resume argv before `_spawn`, so a future change *can* ship a rule-breaking argv and only the tests (if updated to match) would notice.

Two clean options:

1. **Wire it in** — validate in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` before including the `-- …` tail (inert on failure, matching the gate philosophy):

```dart
if (resume && resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sid])) ...['--', 'fa', '--session', sid],
```

2. **Fix the comment** — drop the defense-in-depth sentence and document that the rules are pinned by `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` snapshots only.

Option 1 makes the stated guarantee real; option 2 stops the comment from misleading the next maintainer. Either resolves this.

---

### Thread 10 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: typo — "detected server" should be "detached server"**

This PR changed "detached server" to "detected server" in the herdr intro. herdr's defining trait is the *detached* server process (it owns agent PTYs), not a "detected" one — and the sentence is about architecture, not screen detection. One-word revert:

```markdown
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detached server, session restore,
```

---

### Thread 11 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc line is stale post-rework — the transport is no longer a `Process.run` closure**

The rework (kill-on-timeout, per the discussion) replaced the `Process.run`-backed spawn in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` with `Process.start` + a 5s kill window. This docs line still describes the retired implementation:

```markdown
The transport is an injected `Process.run` closure (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`); lib/ stays dart:io-free.
```

Suggest rewording to match the shipped code, e.g. "an injected `Process.start`-backed spawn with a kill-on-timeout window (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`)". Same stale wording appears in the PR description, but the doc is the durable artifact.

---

### Thread 12 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: fire-and-forget spawns can land out of order — pane state can regress until the next transition**

`_spawn` launches each report as an independent unawaited subprocess. Seq is assigned at build time, but delivery order is not guaranteed: a slow earlier report (e.g. boot `idle`, seq N) can arrive *after* a fast later one (run start `working`, seq N+1). Since herdr ignores non-increasing seq, the `idle` is dropped — fine — but the reverse interleaving (fast `working` then slow `idle` is the normal order; the risk is a slow `working` arriving after a later `idle`) can leave the pane showing a stale state until the next transition heals it.

Realistic trigger: boot `idle` immediately followed by a submitted prompt (`working`) — two spawns in the same millisecond-ish window. Impact is transient and self-healing per the fire-and-forget contract, so this doesn't block; if you want ordering, chain the sends (`_pending = _pending.then((_) => _send(argv))`) — still fire-and-forget, but serialized. Worth a conscious decision either way.

---

### Thread 13 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `release()` has no once-guard — "exactly once" rests entirely on the teardown call sites**

The reporter's release is documented as "sent exactly once, on real quit only," but `release()` itself is not idempotent — a second invocation spawns a second `release-agent` report. Today both paths into `_teardownAfterRepl` (`run()`'s finally and `_wireServeTeardown`) are mutually exclusive per process, so the invariant holds by call-site discipline only.

A one-line guard inside the reporter would make the invariant robust against a future third teardown path or a double-invoked shutdown:

```dart
Future<void> release() async {
  if (!_active || _released) return;
  _released = true;
  await _send(releaseArgs(seq: _nextSeq()));
}
```

Defense in depth only — no current double-send path found.

---

### Thread 14 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `Process.start` without draining stdout/stderr — a chatty herdr blocks on a full pipe until the kill window**

The spawn closure starts herdr and awaits only `exitCode`; the child's stdout/stderr streams are never read or redirected. If a (current or future) herdr build prints more than the OS pipe buffer (~64 KiB) for a report, the subprocess blocks on write, `exitCode` never completes, and every report burns the full 5s kill window — one killed process per transition, silently.

herdr 0.8.2's `pane report-*` presumably emits nothing, so this is latent, not live. Cheap hardening:

```dart
final process = await Process.start(
  argv.first,
  argv.sublist(1),
  mode: ProcessStartMode.detachedWithStdio, // or attach a draining listener
);
process.stdout.drain();
process.stderr.drain();
```

…or `Process.run` (which drains internally) composed with an explicit kill timer. Either keeps the kill-on-timeout contract intact.

# herdr integration

[herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr) is a terminal multiplexer built
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detected server, session restore,
remote machines), marks every pane `working / blocked / idle / done`, and
exposes a CLI + socket API so agents can spawn panes and wait on each
other. fa is a supported herdr agent through three seams — the pane-state
reporter (v2, primary), a skill install target, and session resume. The
screen-scrape detection manifest survives as a demoted second tier.

## 1. Pane state — `HerdrReporter` (v2, self-report)

fa reports its own pane state to herdr: a session running inside a herdr
pane keeps herdr's record of that pane true for the whole life of the pane
and releases cleanly on exit. The v1 framing — herdr detects fa by
screen-scraping a detection manifest merged upstream — is retracted: that
manifest never landed in herdrdev/herdr, and a real fa session in a herdr
pane sat at `agent_status: "unknown"` while these docs claimed support.

`HerdrReporter` (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`) owns exactly one job:
reporting the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` to the binary named by
`HERDR_BIN_PATH`. Every report is one fire-and-forget subprocess of
`"$HERDR_BIN_PATH" pane …` with a short timeout, silent on failure — a
dead herdr is indistinguishable from no herdr (no retry, no queue, no log
line, no user-visible output).

**Gate** — the reporter is active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND
`HERDR_PANE_ID` is set and charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`; the colon
is part of the accepted set because herdr's real ids are `window:pane`)
AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is set, absolute, and argv-safe, AND the kill switch
is not engaged (`FA_HERDR=0`). herdr exports the vars to every pane
process,
so the CLI reads its own process env; `FA_HERDR=0` turns the integration
off per-pane or per-machine. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no
herdr: the reporter is constructed inert and spawns nothing for the
process lifetime. A herdr-less machine regresses nothing.

**State machine** (subject: fa's own pane, as herdr records it):

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1483._

> ℹ️ **8 resolved thread(s) excluded; 3 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 9 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `resumeArgvValid` is dead production code — the "defense in depth" claim is false**

This validator is never called anywhere in `lib/` or `bin/` (only the unit tests exercise it), yet the doc comment states the check "exists as defense in depth so a future change cannot ship a rule-breaking argv." It provides no such defense: nothing in the argv builders (`reportStateArgs`, `sessionSwitchArgs`) validates the resume argv before `_spawn`, so a future change *can* ship a rule-breaking argv and only the tests (if updated to match) would notice.

Two clean options:

1. **Wire it in** — validate in `state()`/`sessionSwitch()` before including the `-- …` tail (inert on failure, matching the gate philosophy):

```dart
if (resume && resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sid])) ...['--', 'fa', '--session', sid],
```

2. **Fix the comment** — drop the defense-in-depth sentence and document that the rules are pinned by `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` snapshots only.

Option 1 makes the stated guarantee real; option 2 stops the comment from misleading the next maintainer. Either resolves this.

---

### Thread 10 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: typo — "detected server" should be "detached server"**

This PR changed "detached server" to "detected server" in the herdr intro. herdr's defining trait is the *detached* server process (it owns agent PTYs), not a "detected" one — and the sentence is about architecture, not screen detection. One-word revert:

```markdown
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detached server, session restore,
```

---

### Thread 11 — `docs/integrations/herdr.md`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: doc line is stale post-rework — the transport is no longer a `Process.run` closure**

The rework (kill-on-timeout, per the discussion) replaced the `Process.run`-backed spawn in `bin/fah_runapp.dart` with `Process.start` + a 5s kill window. This docs line still describes the retired implementation:

```markdown
The transport is an injected `Process.run` closure (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`); lib/ stays dart:io-free.
```

Suggest rewording to match the shipped code, e.g. "an injected `Process.start`-backed spawn with a kill-on-timeout window (`bin/fah_runapp.dart`)". Same stale wording appears in the PR description, but the doc is the durable artifact.

---

### Thread 12 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: fire-and-forget spawns can land out of order — pane state can regress until the next transition**

`_spawn` launches each report as an independent unawaited subprocess. Seq is assigned at build time, but delivery order is not guaranteed: a slow earlier report (e.g. boot `idle`, seq N) can arrive *after* a fast later one (run start `working`, seq N+1). Since herdr ignores non-increasing seq, the `idle` is dropped — fine — but the reverse interleaving (fast `working` then slow `idle` is the normal order; the risk is a slow `working` arriving after a later `idle`) can leave the pane showing a stale state until the next transition heals it.

Realistic trigger: boot `idle` immediately followed by a submitted prompt (`working`) — two spawns in the same millisecond-ish window. Impact is transient and self-healing per the fire-and-forget contract, so this doesn't block; if you want ordering, chain the sends (`_pending = _pending.then((_) => _send(argv))`) — still fire-and-forget, but serialized. Worth a conscious decision either way.

---

### Thread 13 — `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `release()` has no once-guard — "exactly once" rests entirely on the teardown call sites**

The reporter's release is documented as "sent exactly once, on real quit only," but `release()` itself is not idempotent — a second invocation spawns a second `release-agent` report. Today both paths into `_teardownAfterRepl` (`run()`'s finally and `_wireServeTeardown`) are mutually exclusive per process, so the invariant holds by call-site discipline only.

A one-line guard inside the reporter would make the invariant robust against a future third teardown path or a double-invoked shutdown:

```dart
Future<void> release() async {
  if (!_active || _released) return;
  _released = true;
  await _send(releaseArgs(seq: _nextSeq()));
}
```

Defense in depth only — no current double-send path found.

---

### Thread 14 — `bin/fah_runapp.dart`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
💡 **SUGGESTION: `Process.start` without draining stdout/stderr — a chatty herdr blocks on a full pipe until the kill window**

The spawn closure starts herdr and awaits only `exitCode`; the child's stdout/stderr streams are never read or redirected. If a (current or future) herdr build prints more than the OS pipe buffer (~64 KiB) for a report, the subprocess blocks on write, `exitCode` never completes, and every report burns the full 5s kill window — one killed process per transition, silently.

herdr 0.8.2's `pane report-*` presumably emits nothing, so this is latent, not live. Cheap hardening:

```dart
final process = await Process.start(
  argv.first,
  argv.sublist(1),
  mode: ProcessStartMode.detachedWithStdio, // or attach a draining listener
);
process.stdout.drain();
process.stderr.drain();
```

…or `Process.run` (which drains internally) composed with an explicit kill timer. Either keeps the kill-on-timeout contract intact.

---

# herdr integration

[herdr](https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr) is a terminal multiplexer built
for coding agents: it owns agent PTYs (detected server, session restore,
remote machines), marks every pane `working / blocked / idle / done`, and
exposes a CLI + socket API so agents can spawn panes and wait on each
other. fa is a supported herdr agent through three seams — the pane-state
reporter (v2, primary), a skill install target, and session resume. The
screen-scrape detection manifest survives as a demoted second tier.

## 1. Pane state — `HerdrReporter` (v2, self-report)

fa reports its own pane state to herdr: a session running inside a herdr
pane keeps herdr's record of that pane true for the whole life of the pane
and releases cleanly on exit. The v1 framing — herdr detects fa by
screen-scraping a detection manifest merged upstream — is retracted: that
manifest never landed in herdrdev/herdr, and a real fa session in a herdr
pane sat at `agent_status: "unknown"` while these docs claimed support.

`HerdrReporter` (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`) owns exactly one job:
reporting the pane named by `HERDR_PANE_ID` to the binary named by
`HERDR_BIN_PATH`. Every report is one fire-and-forget subprocess of
`"$HERDR_BIN_PATH" pane …` with a short timeout, silent on failure — a
dead herdr is indistinguishable from no herdr (no retry, no queue, no log
line, no user-visible output).

**Gate** — the reporter is active only when `HERDR_ENV=1` AND
`HERDR_PANE_ID` is set and charset-valid (`[A-Za-z0-9._:-]+`; the colon
is part of the accepted set because herdr's real ids are `window:pane`)
AND `HERDR_BIN_PATH` is set, absolute, and argv-safe, AND the kill switch
is not engaged (`FA_HERDR=0`). herdr exports the vars to every pane
process,
so the CLI reads its own process env; `FA_HERDR=0` turns the integration
off per-pane or per-machine. Any unmet condition is byte-identical to no
herdr: the reporter is constructed inert and spawns nothing for the
process lifetime. A herdr-less machine regresses nothing.

**State machine** (subject: fa's own pane, as herdr records it):
