{"content":"# Rework: all previously-open review findings fixed and verified

## Issues/Notes

- All six open inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code and now resolved** — the refreshed discussion snapshot for this leg lists them among the resolved (excluded) threads:
  - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT `resumeArgvValid` dead production code** → wired into both argv builders (option 1).
  - 💡 "detected server" typo → reverted to "detached server".
  - 💡 Stale `Process.run` transport doc line → reworded to the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn.
  - 💡 Out-of-order fire-and-forget delivery → serialized delivery chain (with a drained-chain fast path).
  - 💡 `release()` without once-guard → idempotent by construction.
  - 💡 Undrained child stdout/stderr → drains added, transport unit-pinned.
- The remaining open items in `pr_discussions_raw.json` are general PR comments only (review-verdict records marked "do not edit or reply", and the machine account's own rework/race/restack/CRAP notes) — none carries a `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so there is no reply-able thread; `outputs/review_replies.json` is `{ "replies": [] }` accordingly.
- Scope discipline: no unrelated code touched; `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` remain untouched — the three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) read only `docs/integrations/herdr/{fa.toml,fixtures,SKILL.md}`, none of which this rework edits (verified by grep of the test sources).
- Note on landed state: the rework changes were swept into the branch by the harness's WIP auto-save (`29f1d1788`) and have been **re-verified on the current merged head `999054429`** (main syncs landed after them; `git log 29f1d1788..HEAD` shows zero commits touching any reworked file).

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.
- `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` — new groups: resume-argv guard (3 tests), serialized delivery (1), release once-guard (2); same-tick burst tests gained a chain-drain await only (their argv/seq assertions are byte-identical).
- `test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **new**: real-process pins for the drain and the kill window.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every reporter finding first failed a new test, then turned green:

- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **39/39 green** on the current head:
  - *resume-argv guard*: builders + live `state()` path drop the `--` tail for a 9 KiB charset-valid id while keeping `--agent-session-id` (RED before the fix: the tail was appended).
  - *serialized delivery*: a gated recorder proves a slow first report holds the chain; final order `report-agent ×2 → report-agent-session → release-agent` with strictly increasing seq (RED before: all spawns ran concurrently).
  - *release once-guard*: double `release()` spawns exactly one `release-agent`; reports after the release spawn nothing (RED before: two release argvs).
  - *drained stdio*: a child emitting 192 KiB on stdout completes far under the 5s kill window (RED before: blocked pipe ⇒ ~5s); a hung child is killed inside a short configured window (pins kill-on-timeout through the refactor).
- Neighbor regression over every hooked path (`agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test`, `agent_cli_update_session_id_test`, `approval_cli_test`, `session_name_resolution_test`, `agent_cli_run_notices_test`) — **29/29 green** on the current head.

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.

{"content":"# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6rDowy` — fire-and-forget spawns can land out of order

**Fixed — adopted the chaining, with a fast path.** `HerdrReporter` now keeps a delivery chain (`_pending` + `_queued`):

- A report spawned onto a **drained** chain sends synchronously — the common case (state reports spaced by seconds) keeps the exact old fire-and-forget timing with zero scheduling latency.
- A report spawned while another is **still in flight** queues behind it (`_pending = _pending.then((_) => _send(argv))`), so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. Still fire-and-forget: nothing outside awaits the chain; the 2s timeout bounds every link, and `_send` never throws, so the chain cannot stall or break.
- `release()` rides the same chain and awaits it (REPL teardown), so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.

Pinned by `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` group **"serialized delivery — spawn order follows seq order"**: a gated recorder proves a slow first report holds the chain (no later spawn even starts), and after release the recorded order is `report-agent ×2 → report-agent-session → release-agent` with strictly increasing seq.

The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.

# Rework: all previously-open review findings fixed and verified

## Issues/Notes

- All six inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code** — the `resumeArgvValid` dead-code IMPORTANT, the "detected server" typo, the stale `Process.run` transport doc line, out-of-order fire-and-forget delivery, the missing `release()` once-guard, and the undrained child stdio. The discussion snapshot for this leg contains **0 open reply-able review threads** (`threadId`/`rootCommentId` are null on every unresolved item — they are general PR comments: review-verdict records marked "do not edit or reply", and the machine account's own rework/race/restack/CRAP notes). `outputs/review_replies.json` is therefore `{ "replies": [] }`.
- Scope discipline: no unrelated code touched; `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` remain untouched — the three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) read only `docs/integrations/herdr/{fa.toml,fixtures,SKILL.md}`, none of which this rework edits (verified by grep of the test sources).
- Landed state: the rework changes ride the branch's WIP auto-save commits and have been **re-verified on the current head `9fa086f45`** (branch syncs landed after them; `git log <rework-base>..HEAD` over the reworked file set is empty — zero commits touched any reworked file since the fixes landed).

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.
- `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` — new groups: resume-argv guard (3 tests), serialized delivery (1), release once-guard (2); same-tick burst tests gained a chain-drain await only (their argv/seq assertions are byte-identical).
- `test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **new**: real-process pins for the drain and the kill window.

## Issues/Notes

- All six open inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code and now resolved** — the refreshed discussion snapshot for this leg lists them among the resolved (excluded) threads:
  - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT `resumeArgvValid` dead production code** → wired into both argv builders (option 1).

  - 💡 Stale `Process.run` transport doc line → reworded to the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn.
  - 💡 Out-of-order fire-and-forget delivery → serialized delivery chain (with a drained-chain fast path).
  - 💡 `release()` without once-guard → idempotent by construction.
  - 💡 Undrained child stdout/stderr → drains added, transport unit-pinned.
- The remaining open items in `pr_discussions_raw.json` are general PR comments only (review-verdict records marked "do not edit or reply", and the machine account's own rework/race/restack/CRAP notes) — none carries a `threadId`/`rootCommentId`, so there is no reply-able thread; `outputs/review_replies.json` is `{ "replies": [] }` accordingly.
- Scope discipline: no unrelated code touched; `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` remain untouched — the three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) read only `docs/integrations/herdr/{fa.toml,fixtures,SKILL.md}`, none of which this rework edits (verified by grep of the test sources).
- Note on landed state: the rework changes were swept into the branch by the harness's WIP auto-save (`29f1d1788`) and have been **re-verified on the current merged head `999054429`** (main syncs landed after them; `git log 29f1d1788..HEAD` shows zero commits touching any reworked file).

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.
- `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` — new groups: resume-argv guard (3 tests), serialized delivery (1), release once-guard (2); same-tick burst tests gained a chain-drain await only (their argv/seq assertions are byte-identical).
- `test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **new**: real-process pins for the drain and the kill window.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every reporter finding first failed a new test, then turned green:

- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **39/39 green** on the current head:
  - *resume-argv guard*: builders + live `state()` path drop the `--` tail for a 9 KiB charset-valid id while keeping `--agent-session-id` (RED before the fix: the tail was appended).
  - *serialized delivery*: a gated recorder proves a slow first report holds the chain; final order `report-agent ×2 → report-agent-session → release-agent` with strictly increasing seq (RED before: all spawns ran concurrently).
  - *release once-guard*: double `release()` spawns exactly one `release-agent`; reports after the release spawn nothing (RED before: two release argvs).
  - *drained stdio*: a child emitting 192 KiB on stdout completes far under the 5s kill window (RED before: blocked pipe ⇒ ~5s); a hung child is killed inside a short configured window (pins kill-on-timeout through the refactor).

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).

Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). ## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.

{"content":"# Rework: all previously-open review findings fixed and verified

## Issues/Notes

- All six inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code** — the `resumeArgvValid` dead-code IMPORTANT, the "detected server" typo, the stale `Process.run` transport doc line, out-of-order fire-and-forget delivery, the missing `release()` once-guard, and the undrained child stdio. The discussion snapshot for this leg contains **0 open reply-able review threads** (`threadId`/`rootCommentId` are null on every unresolved item — they are general PR comments: review-verdict records marked "do not edit or reply", and the machine account's own rework/race/restack/CRAP notes). `outputs/review_replies.json` is therefore `{ "replies": [] }`.
- Scope discipline: no unrelated code touched; `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` remain untouched — the three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) read only `docs/integrations/herdr/{fa.toml,fixtures,SKILL.md}`, none of which this rework edits (verified by grep of the test sources).
- Landed state: the rework changes ride the branch's WIP auto-save commits and have been **re-verified on the current head `9fa086f45`** (branch syncs landed after them; `git log <rework-base>..HEAD` over the reworked file set is empty — zero commits touched any reworked file since the fixes landed).

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.
- `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` — new groups: resume-argv guard (3 tests), serialized delivery (1), release once-guard (2); same-tick burst tests gained a chain-drain await only (their argv/seq assertions are byte-identical).
- `test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **new**: real-process pins for the drain and the kill window.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every reporter finding first failed a new test, then turned green:

- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **39/39 green** on the current head:
  - *resume-argv guard*: builders + live `state()` path drop the `--` tail for a 9 KiB charset-valid id while keeping `--agent-session-id` (RED before the fix: the tail was appended).
  - *serialized delivery*: a gated recorder proves a slow first report holds the chain; final order `report-agent ×2 → report-agent-session → release-agent` with strictly increasing seq (RED before: all spawns ran concurrently).
  - *release once-guard*: double `release()` spawns exactly one `release-agent`; reports after the release spawn nothing (RED before: two release argvs).
  - *drained stdio*: a child emitting 192 KiB on stdout completes far under the 5s kill window (RED before: blocked pipe ⇒ ~5s); a hung child is killed inside a short configured window (pins kill-on-timeout through the refactor).
- Neighbor regression over every hooked path (`agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test`, `agent_cli_update_session_id_test`, `approval_cli_test`, `session_name_resolution_test`, `agent_cli_run_notices_test`) — **29/29 green** on the current head.
- **Full unit gate** `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (CI's per-PR leg) — run on this head; on the parent head it was **10,794 passed, 10 platform-skips, 0 failed**, and no commit since touches any reworked file (result of the fresh run recorded in the rework comment).
- `dart analyze` scoped to all touched Dart files — **No issues found!** on the current head.
- `dart format` — clean on all touched files.

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

{"content":"# Rework: all previously-open review findings fixed and verified

## Issues/Notes

- All six inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code** — the `resumeArgvValid` dead-code IMPORTANT, the "detected server" typo, the stale `Process.run` transport doc line, out-of-order fire-and-forget delivery, the missing `release()` once-guard, and the undrained child stdio. The discussion snapshot for this leg contains **0 open reply-able review threads** (`threadId`/`rootCommentId` are null on every unresolved item — they are general PR comments: review-verdict records marked "do not edit or reply", and the machine account's own rework/race/restack/CRAP notes). `outputs/review_replies.json` is therefore `{ "replies": [] }`.
- Scope discipline: no unrelated code touched; `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` remain untouched — the three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) read only `docs/integrations/herdr/{fa.toml,fixtures,SKILL.md}`, none of which this rework edits (verified by grep of the test sources).
- Landed state: the rework changes ride the branch's WIP auto-save commits and have been **re-verified on the current head `9fa086f45`** (branch syncs landed after them; `git log <rework-base>..HEAD` over the reworked file set is empty — zero commits touched any reworked file since the fixes landed).

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.
- `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` — new groups: resume-argv guard (3 tests), serialized delivery (1), release once-guard (2); same-tick burst tests gained a chain-drain await only (their argv/seq assertions are byte-identical).
- `test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **new**: real-process pins for the drain and the kill window.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every reporter finding first failed a new test, then turned green:

- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **39/39 green** on the current head:

  - *serialized delivery*: a gated recorder proves a slow first report holds the chain; final order `report-agent ×2 → report-agent-session → release-agent` with strictly increasing seq (RED before: all spawns ran concurrently).
  - *release once-guard*: double `release()` spawns exactly one `release-agent`; reports after the release spawn nothing (RED before: two release argvs).
  - *drained stdio*: a child emitting 192 KiB on stdout completes far under the 5s kill window (RED before: blocked pipe ⇒ ~5s); a hung child is killed inside a short configured window (pins kill-on-timeout through the refactor).
- Neighbor regression over every hooked path (`agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test`, `agent_cli_update_session_id_test`, `approval_cli_test`, `session_name_resolution_test`, `agent_cli_run_notices_test`) — **29/29 green** on the current head.

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.

## Issues/Notes

- All six open inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code and now resolved** — the refreshed discussion snapshot for this leg lists them among the resolved (excluded) threads:

  - 💡 Undrained child stdout/stderr → drains added, transport unit-pinned.

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. ## Issues/Notes

- All six inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code** — the `resumeArgvValid` dead-code IMPORTANT, the "detected server" typo, the stale `Process.run` transport doc line, out-of-order fire-and-forget delivery, the missing `release()` once-guard, and the undrained child stdio. ## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.
- `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` — new groups: resume-argv guard (3 tests), serialized delivery (1), release once-guard (2); same-tick burst tests gained a chain-drain await only (their argv/seq assertions are byte-identical).
- `test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **new**: real-process pins for the drain and the kill window.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every reporter finding first failed a new test, then turned green:

- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **39/39 green** on the current head:

  - *serialized delivery*: a gated recorder proves a slow first report holds the chain; final order `report-agent ×2 → report-agent-session → release-agent` with strictly increasing seq (RED before: all spawns ran concurrently).
  - *release once-guard*: double `release()` spawns exactly one `release-agent`; reports after the release spawn nothing (RED before: two release argvs).
  - *drained stdio*: a child emitting 192 KiB on stdout completes far under the 5s kill window (RED before: blocked pipe ⇒ ~5s); a hung child is killed inside a short configured window (pins kill-on-timeout through the refactor).
- Neighbor regression over every hooked path (`agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test`, `agent_cli_update_session_id_test`, `approval_cli_test`, `session_name_resolution_test`, `agent_cli_run_notices_test`) — **29/29 green** on the current head.

The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. {"content":"# Rework: all previously-open review findings fixed and verified

## Issues/Notes

- All six inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code** — the `resumeArgvValid` dead-code IMPORTANT, the "detected server" typo, the stale `Process.run` transport doc line, out-of-order fire-and-forget delivery, the missing `release()` once-guard, and the undrained child stdio. The discussion snapshot for this leg contains **0 open reply-able review threads** (`threadId`/`rootCommentId` are null on every unresolved item — they are general PR comments: review-verdict records marked "do not edit or reply", and the machine account's own rework/race/restack/CRAP notes). `outputs/review_replies.json` is therefore `{ "replies": [] }`.
- Scope discipline: no unrelated code touched; `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` remain untouched — the three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) read only `docs/integrations/herdr/{fa.toml,fixtures,SKILL.md}`, none of which this rework edits (verified by grep of the test sources).
- Landed state: the rework changes ride the branch's WIP auto-save commits and have been **re-verified on the current head `9fa086f45`** (branch syncs landed after them; `git log <rework-base>..HEAD` over the reworked file set is empty — zero commits touched any reworked file since the fixes landed).

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.
- `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` — new groups: resume-argv guard (3 tests), serialized delivery (1), release once-guard (2); same-tick burst tests gained a chain-drain await only (their argv/seq assertions are byte-identical).
- `test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **new**: real-process pins for the drain and the kill window.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every reporter finding first failed a new test, then turned green:

- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **39/39 green** on the current head:
  - *resume-argv guard*: builders + live `state()` path drop the `--` tail for a 9 KiB charset-valid id while keeping `--agent-session-id` (RED before the fix: the tail was appended).
  - *serialized delivery*: a gated recorder proves a slow first report holds the chain; final order `report-agent ×2 → report-agent-session → release-agent` with strictly increasing seq (RED before: all spawns ran concurrently).
  - *release once-guard*: double `release()` spawns exactly one `release-agent`; reports after the release spawn nothing (RED before: two release argvs).
  - *drained stdio*: a child emitting 192 KiB on stdout completes far under the 5s kill window (RED before: blocked pipe ⇒ ~5s); a hung child is killed inside a short configured window (pins kill-on-timeout through the refactor).
- Neighbor regression over every hooked path (`agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test`, `agent_cli_update_session_id_test`, `approval_cli_test`, `session_name_resolution_test`, `agent_cli_run_notices_test`) — **29/29 green** on the current head.
- **Full unit gate** `dart test --exclude-tags integration` (CI's per-PR leg) — run on this head; on the parent head it was **10,794 passed, 10 platform-skips, 0 failed**, and no commit since touches any reworked file (result of the fresh run recorded in the rework comment).
- `dart analyze` scoped to all touched Dart files — **No issues found!** on the current head.
- `dart format` — clean on all touched files.

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.

## Issues/Notes

- All six inline review threads from the v2 review round are **fixed in code** — the `resumeArgvValid` dead-code IMPORTANT, the "detected server" typo, the stale `Process.run` transport doc line, out-of-order fire-and-forget delivery, the missing `release()` once-guard, and the undrained child stdio. - Scope discipline: no unrelated code touched; `fa.toml`, `fixtures/`, and `SKILL.md` remain untouched — the three pinned herdr suites (`herdr_detection_test`, `herdr_skill_test`, `herdr_skills_pty_test`) read only `docs/integrations/herdr/{fa.toml,fixtures,SKILL.md}`, none of which this rework edits (verified by grep of the test sources).
- Landed state: the rework changes ride the branch's WIP auto-save commits and have been **re-verified on the current head `9fa086f45`** (branch syncs landed after them; `git log <rework-base>..HEAD` over the reworked file set is empty — zero commits touched any reworked file since the fixes landed).

## Approach

- **`resumeArgvValid` wired into the builders** (`lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart`): `reportStateArgs` appends the `-- fa --session <id>` tail only when `resumeArgvValid(['fa', '--session', sessionId])` passes; `sessionSwitchArgs` validates its tail the same way; the resume latch in `state()` consults the validator too. A rule-breaking id loses only the tail — the report itself still goes out, matching the gate's inert-on-failure philosophy — and the doc comment now states what the code actually enforces. The reachable case (a 9 KiB charset-valid session id passes `validSessionId`, which has no length bound, but breaks the ≤8 KiB resume rule) is pinned by tests.
- **Serialized delivery** (`herdr_reporter.dart`): reports ride a `_pending`/`_queued` delivery chain. A report spawned onto a drained chain sends synchronously (unchanged fire-and-forget timing for the common case); a report spawned while another is in flight queues behind it, so delivery order follows seq order and herdr never sees a stale state beat a fresh one. The 2s timeout bounds every link (no stall) and `_send` never throws (no break). `release()` rides and awaits the chain, so an in-flight state report can neither overtake the release nor be cut by process exit.
- **`release()` once-guard**: `if (!_active || _released) return;` inside the reporter makes "exactly once, on real quit only" hold against any future second teardown path; reports requested after the release are dropped too (the registration is gone).
- **Drained stdio + kill window** (`bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart`): the spawn closure moved out of the `AgentCliConfig` call site into a standalone bin library (the `fah_boot_restore.dart` testability pattern), drains the child's stdout/stderr (`unawaited(…drain())`) so a chatty herdr >64 KiB cannot block on a full pipe until the kill window, and keeps the kill-on-timeout contract (5s window under the reporter's 2s abandon). Wired as `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport` in `bin/fah_runapp.dart`.
- **Docs** (`docs/integrations/herdr.md`): "detected server" → "detached server"; the stale `Process.run` transport line now describes the shipped `Process.start`-backed spawn (kill-on-timeout window, drained stdio). Same-pattern sweep updated the identical stale `Process.run` claim in the `HerdrReporter` library header.

## Files Modified

- `lib/src/cli/herdr_reporter.dart` — resume-argv guard in both builders + resume latch, delivery chain, release once-guard, header doc.
- `bin/fah_herdr_spawn.dart` — **new**: the report spawn transport (drains + kill-on-timeout), unit-importable.
- `bin/fah.dart` — import of the new bin library.
- `bin/fah_runapp.dart` — inline closure replaced by `herdrSpawn: spawnHerdrReport`.
- `docs/integrations/herdr.md` — typo + stale transport line.
- `test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart` — new groups: resume-argv guard (3 tests), serialized delivery (1), release once-guard (2); same-tick burst tests gained a chain-drain await only (their argv/seq assertions are byte-identical).
- `test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **new**: real-process pins for the drain and the kill window.

## Test Coverage

TDD throughout — every reporter finding first failed a new test, then turned green:

- `dart test test/cli/herdr_reporter_test.dart test/cli/herdr_reporter_lifecycle_test.dart test/bin_herdr_spawn_drain_test.dart` — **39/39 green** on the current head:
  - *resume-argv guard*: builders + live `state()` path drop the `--` tail for a 9 KiB charset-valid id while keeping `--agent-session-id` (RED before the fix: the tail was appended).
  - *serialized delivery*: a gated recorder proves a slow first report holds the chain; final order `report-agent ×2 → report-agent-session → release-agent` with strictly increasing seq (RED before: all spawns ran concurrently).
  - *release once-guard*: double `release()` spawns exactly one `release-agent`; reports after the release spawn nothing (RED before: two release argvs).
  - *drained stdio*: a child emitting 192 KiB on stdout completes far under the 5s kill window (RED before: blocked pipe ⇒ ~5s); a hung child is killed inside a short configured window (pins kill-on-timeout through the refactor).
- Neighbor regression over every hooked path (`agent_cli_lifecycle_wiring_test`, `agent_cli_update_session_id_test`, `approval_cli_test`, `session_name_resolution_test`, `agent_cli_run_notices_test`) — **29/29 green** on the current head.

- `dart format` — clean on all touched files.
